subject: RE: Conversation pause — sustained token latency on streaming chat
messages:
From: Ethan Shaw <ethan@wavepay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@wavepay.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Conversation pause — sustained token latency on streaming chat

Hi Karthik / Laura,

We started seeing sustained pauses (~4-7s) in our live chat streaming responses this morning across multiple regions. The UI shows partial chunks then a long gap before completion — it’s impacting our agent assist product. We correlated to the Redwood streaming endpoint (model: rwd-gpt-large-stream). Attached are a short metric dump and a client trace.

What we observed: 
- Spike in token delivery latency starting 08:40 PDT, sustained for ~35 minutes.
- Few requests returned partial streaming events and then closed the connection.

Impact: ~12% of live sessions showed pauses >3s which caused agents to reload the chat.

Can you confirm this is on your side and advise immediate mitigations we can apply while you triage?

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Shaw
Head of Product Operations, WavePay
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Shaw <ethan@wavepay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Conversation pause — sustained token latency on streaming chat

Thanks for the report, Ethan — we’re on it. 

Quick notes from triage: our early telemetry shows intermittent heartbeat-throttle events at the edge layer for the US-west shard that caused delayed token flushes to the client. We are treating this as high priority and have a small on-call team investigating kernel selection changes that rolled out to a subset of instances earlier this morning.

Immediate mitigations you can try while we continue: 
- Switch to non-streaming (single shot) generation temporarily for the most latency-sensitive flows; this avoids incremental flush behavior. 
- Reduce max_tokens to 128 for interactive sessions to shorten processing windows. 
- Add a client-side reconnect/backoff (incremental 250ms) to tolerate short stalls.

I’ve flagged JIRA-INC-9482 and shared the trace artifacts with engineering. Attaching our mitigation playbook with quick steps (see attachment). We’ll follow up with a timeline and root cause.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Shaw <ethan@wavepay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Conversation pause — sustained token latency on streaming chat

Ethan — quick follow-up from the on-call runbook: 

What we changed (temporary):
- Rolling revert of the kernel selection tweak on the US-west streaming pool at 09:52 PDT; rollout completed 10:00 PDT.
- Throttling rule on the shard was relaxed to allow larger heartbeats for 20 minutes.

Client-side workarounds we recommend while you validate:
1) If you can toggle streaming to a single-response path in feature flags, do that for the next 1–2 hours.
2) If not possible, apply a client-side chunk-guard: if no token arrives in 1.5s, re-open the websocket once (preserve conversation state).

Attachments included: stream-trace-20270611.zip (server traces), wavepay-metrics.csv (your posted metrics annotated).

We’re watching for reoccurrence and will keep you posted.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Shaw <ethan@wavepay.com>, Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@wavepay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: token pacing regression and next steps (WavePay)

Hi Ethan / Jordan,

Thanks for your patience while we completed the investigation. Below is a concise post-incident summary and required actions on both sides.

Incident timeline (summary):
- 08:39 PDT: First elevated token latency observed in edge metrics for US-west shard.
- 08:41 PDT: Canary kernel selection tweak rolled to small subset (internal rollout).
- 08:45 PDT: Telemetry shows increased KV cache miss amplification on affected instances.
- 09:52 PDT: Revert of kernel tweak initiated after correlation with latency spikes.
- 10:00 PDT: Revert completed; latency returned to normal by 10:07 PDT.

Root cause: an internal kernel selection change altered attention kernel invocation for the rwd-gpt-large-stream model in low-latency mode which, for some request shapes, increased memory pressure and caused delayed token flushes at the edge. This manifested as sustained token pacing delays and intermittent partial-streamed closures.

Preventative and remediation actions (we will do):
- Disable the kernel selection heuristic in autopilot for streaming pools until additional regression tests are added (complete).
- Add a synthetic streaming regression test in our CI that simulates short interactive sessions (in progress; target deployment 2027-07-05).
- Improve telemetry to emit early warning when token flush latency > 500ms for more than 10% of sessions (action item: KT-112).

Actions for WavePay (recommended, optional):
- Keep a lightweight feature-flag route to fall back to single-shot responses for agent-critical flows.
- Implement client-side chunk-guard (ben’s suggestion) to auto-reconnect once after a 1.5s stall.

Compensation / next steps: 
- We’ve opened HS-4521 in HubSpot to track credits for the incident window and will follow up with your account team by EOD tomorrow.
- JIRA-INC-9482 contains the full trace set and remediation checklist.

Attachments: rw-mitigation-playbook-v2.pdf (includes temporary feature flag example and reconnection pseudocode).

If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-minute technical walkthrough with our on-call engineers later this week.

Best,
Karthik
From: Ethan Shaw <ethan@wavepay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@wavepay.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident summary: token pacing regression and next steps (WavePay)

Karthik — appreciate the clear timeline and the playbook. We validated the suggested client guard and saw a drop in visible stalls to <1% in our canary. The single-shot fallback is already behind a feature flag so we’ll keep that on standby.

Please proceed with the HubSpot credit action and let us know availability for a walkthrough Thursday or Friday.

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Shaw
Head of Product Operations, WavePay
